item.title: The Oki Islands: A UNESCO Geopark in the Sea of Japan — Guide
item.description: The Oki Islands lie some 50 kilometres out in the Sea of Japan, a cluster of four inhabited islands and many islets that form a UNESCO Global Geopark. Their volcanic and geological history has produced dramatic scenery: the Kuniga coast on Nishinoshima, where the sheer Matengai cliff drops 250 metres straight into the sea and horses and cattle graze freely on the clifftops, is among the most spectacular coastlines in Japan.
